sections.COMMENTS:
This Composite Source straddles the area in southern Calabria between the southern shoulder of the Serre Mts. (to the north) and the Gioia Tauro plain (to the south), along the Nicotera-Gioiosa Ionica Line. This source is a high-angle, SW-dipping, left-lateral strike-slip fault, part of the strike-slip system that dissects and advances the central and southern Calabrian arc toward SE.
Historical catalogues (Boschi et al., 2000; Gruppo di Lavoro CPTI, 2004; Guidoboni et al., 2007) report some damaging earthquakes in the western sector of the area, while a 1997 seismic sequence characterized the eastern sector. In particular, this region has been struck by the 7 March 1928 (Mw 5.9, Capo Vaticano) and the 8 September 1905 (Mw 7.1, Calabria) earthquakes.
This source marks a sharp tectonic and topographic shift from the uplands of the Serre Mts. (possibly undergoing faster uplift) to the basin fill of the Gioia Tauro plain and the Dossone della Melia ridge. So far, investigators have concentrated on the structural geology of the northern border of the region, while the present-day tectonic role of the area remains relatively unexplored. Although data are still unclear, we believe that this region is controlled by the south-easterly advancement of the Calabrian Arc toward the Ionian Sea.
A segment of this Source has been associated with the 1928 earthquake. For an in-depth analysis of seismogenic processes in this region, the reader may refer to the relevant Individual Source in this Database.
The strike of this Source was based on that of the mapped regional structures. Also the dip was based on geological and geometrical considerations. Rake is indicative of normal to left-lateral strike-slip faulting, based on regional geological data. The minimum and maximum depth were based on geological and geometrical considerations. Slip rate was inferred from geological observations in adjacent structures that share the same tectonic environment with this Source.
